source.title: Enforcing Orderedness to Improve Feature Consistency
source.authors: Sophie L. Wang; Alex Quach; Nithin Parsan; John J. Yang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE features are consistent across runs and how feature consistency and ordering vary, using stability, orderedness, and SAE stitching rather than the original superposition method.
record.gate_note: The paper tests SAE feature consistency and stitching-based feature completeness, not superposition geometry, polysemanticity, or whether features overlap as nearly orthogonal directions. Toy-model recovery and stability results do not measure the geometry named in V1. The stitching table reports aggregate percentages and does not name the underlying model.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a methods paper proposing O-SAEs. Its absolute results still bear on V5: seed-to-seed stability is well below 1, cross-dataset stability drops further, and stitching finds 34–74% novel features in 4096-wide SAEs. Both show LLM SAE features are not stable or complete units.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that O-SAEs improve orderedness and early-feature stability over Matryoshka baselines, at some cost to later-feature stability. In Appendix D they also claim O-SAEs reduce SAE incompleteness, while conceding 33.8% novel features is still substantial.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a nested-prefix ordered SAE objective and evaluates consistency and feature stitching; it does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method or test its feature-overlap geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that performance is sensitive to prefix distribution and unit sweeping. Empirical stability and orderedness vary by feature prefix, dataset, and seed comparison; some measures change with training progression.

fits_no_version.finding: O-SAEs give higher cross-seed orderedness of dictionary indices than Matryoshka SAEs (near 0.8 on Gemma-2 2B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training objectives can impose a reproducible ordering on SAE features.

fits_no_version.finding: On a Gaussian toy dictionary-learning task (Table 1), seed-to-seed stability is 0.53–0.66 and ground-truth recovery 0.48–0.81 depending on architecture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE recovery of ground-truth sparse dictionaries is incomplete and architecture-dependent in synthetic data.

record.peer_reviewed: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: The LLM evidence is primarily comparative consistency/orderedness measurement, much of it shown in figures without numeric values in the text. Pythia checkpoints are reported after 50M tokens, and some training-progress plots use only n=1 seed pair. The stitching table does not identify the underlying model. The authors note limited hyperparameter sweeps, possible over-regularization if ordering is misspecified, sensitivity to design choices, and higher training cost.
record.rows_left_out: Toy-model Table 1 and appendix toy-model results report recovery, stability, orderedness, and reconstruction metrics, but do not measure any claim version's specified superposition geometry or LLM SAE units. Appendix C training-progress plots are descriptive and include n=1 pair-of-seeds plots; their qualitative observations are noted in method_sensitivity and were not added as separate rows.

untested.parts: No superposition geometry, interference or sparsity transition is measured.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity allocation is measured.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons is not tested; SAE recovery of real-model features is assumed.
Canonicality against the model's own computation (causal use) is not tested; only run-to-run consistency and stitching completeness are.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Numeric cross-seed stability levels for all SAE variants (Fig. 2b axis about 0.3–0.7); only qualitative text.
The underlying model and layer for the stitching experiment are not stated.

record.verdict_notes: This is a methods paper; most rows are own-method-versus-baseline comparisons. V5 evidence comes from the absolute values: imperfect stability across seeds and datasets, and substantial stitching novelty, which replicates Leask et al. The orderedness metric is not a V5 property. Same-seed cross-dataset results reflect shared initialization rather than stability.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure overlapping, nearly orthogonal feature geometry, interference, or a sparsity-dependent transition.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not measure polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.

The study evaluates SAE consistency on LLM activations but does not directly test whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or whether a dictionary recovers sparse underlying features in real models.
Tests run-to-run feature consistency and a stitching-based indicator of feature completeness; does not establish that SAE features are canonical units of the underlying model in general.
Uses dictionary atoms as individual features but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional ones.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured orderedness between SAE dictionaries trained with different seeds.
rows.baseline: Fixed-prefix MSAE and Random-prefix MSAE with 5 groups
rows.value: OSAE has the greatest orderedness, almost reaching an average Ord(D,D′) of 0.8; Fixed MSAE is close to 0.0 for the first 128 features and then rises to around 0.5.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals visualized; numeric interval values not stated.
rows.note: The text describes the comparisons; the plotted values are not given numerically.
rows.check: Orderedness compares the study's own method with baselines. Index ordering is not what V5 names (completeness, stability, canonicality).

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured stability between SAE dictionaries trained with different seeds.
rows.value: OSAE has higher stability for the most significant features.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals visualized; numeric interval values not stated.
rows.note: The result is limited to the early, most significant features.
rows.check: Stated as an OSAE-vs-MSAE comparison. What bears on V5 is the absolute cross-seed stability, which the Fig. 2b axis shows at about 0.3–0.7, not 1. No numbers are given in the text.

source_check.correct: The reported value compares O-SAE performance with Matryoshka baselines. For this comparative value alone, V5 state=cannot_determine; an absolute cross-seed stability result should be recorded separately.
source_check.problem: The comparison is accurate, but the rules exclude standalone own-method comparisons as evidence for the claim.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B

conditions.value: full dictionary; crossover between 1024 and 2048 features

rows.value: OSAE has lower overall average stability than the Matryoshka variants; its prefix-length stability falls below Random MSAE at a crossover between 1024 and 2048 features.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals visualized; numeric interval values not stated.
rows.note: The text reports both lower average stability overall and the crossover at later prefix lengths.
rows.check: Stability declines sharply for later features. The row is framed as a method comparison; the V5-relevant fact is that stability is incomplete.

source_check.correct: O-SAE has lower overall average stability than the Matryoshka variants and crosses below Random MSAE between prefixes 1024 and 2048. For this comparative value alone, V5 state=cannot_determine.
source_check.problem: The row records an own-method comparison rather than absolute stability establishing the degree to which V5 holds.

rows.subject: BatchTopK
rows.operation_detail: Stitched larger-SAE features into a smaller SAE and classified the result by reconstruction effect.
rows.note: A nonzero novel-feature percentage is evidence of features missing from the smaller SAE, against completeness.
rows.check: Completeness is absent: 73.8% of stitched 65536-wide features are novel for BatchTopK. The state should be absent of the version's property, not reversed. The underlying model is unstated.
